findings.description: `escapes` runs `realpathSync` on the committed `node_modules` and its top-level entries only, so a deeper committed symlink reaches the session's live worktree, and so does any committed symlink outside `node_modules`.

`escapes` calls `realpathSync`, which throws a raw ENOENT on a dangling top-level link in a committed `node_modules`, so the gate fails closed with no gate message or report instead of its own refusal.

No test covers the delta's main safety claim, that every environment (nested ones included) is linked before any stage runs, nor the `dirname(local)` guard. The nested `node_modules` test passes whether linking happens before or after the root stages, so a root `build` stage that asserts the nested package's `node_modules` entry already exists would pin the ordering.

The "Every stage and debt capability measures the pinned sha's files…" comment used to sit above `cutGateCheckout`. The delta moved that call to ~L740, so the comment now sits above the `commandStage` helper and describes nothing nearby. Move it above the `capabilityContext`/`cutGateCheckout` lines.

"The parent is a committed directory a stage has not run in yet; still, a link is only ever written under the checkout itself." The "still" hedge leaves the reader to infer the point. It would be clearer as "a committed parent could itself be a link out; check it before writing under it".
In the `linkEnvironment` JSDoc, "so `.vite*` is skipped, and `.cache` with it so a stage writes its cache here" is hard to parse, and it is the only place the `.cache` reason is given.

`linkEnvironment` now does three jobs: it decides whether a committed `node_modules` escapes the checkout, it checks that the parent stays inside, and it creates the links. Splitting the escape guard into its own helper would make it readable and testable on its own.

The two new tests repeat the same `git hash-object -w --stdin` / `update-index --cacheinfo` / `commit` sequence and then mirror the entry into the worktree. That is two uses, so extraction isn't required yet, but a small `commitRawEntry(worktree, mode, content, path)` helper is the obvious move if a third test appears.

Committed symlinks outside `node_modules` (for example `src/feature.test.ts -> <worktree>/src/feature.test.ts`) are checked out as-is into the gate checkout and nothing resolves them, so a stage can read files the live session edits. This gap dates from the detached-checkout commit, not this delta.
